read: partial: abstract, sections 1-3 in full (p.1-6), the results tables and their discussion (p.7-9); appendices skimmed
venue_now: ICLR 2025: the page header reads 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' (p.1); arXiv 2410.12784v2, 5 Apr 2025
what_it_is: A benchmark of LLM-based judges on 350 response pairs in knowledge, reasoning, mathematics and coding, each pairing one objectively correct and one objectively incorrect response sampled from the same strong model (e.g. GPT-4o) on hard existing datasets, so that the pair is hard to tell apart (p.3-4). Each pair is judged twice with the order swapped (p.4). Prompted, fine-tuned and multi-agent judges and reward models are compared (p.1).
source_of_items: responses generated from existing difficult datasets, labelled by objective correctness (p.3-4)
evaluation: judge accuracy at picking the correct response, with order swapped (p.4)
human_validation: n/a: labels come from the source datasets' answers

engtrace_use.sentence: ... and on difficult objective comparisons they do little better than chance [@tan2025judgebench], ...
engtrace_use.explanation: The abstract says 'many strong models (e.g., GPT-4o) performing just slightly better than random guessing' (p.1): GPT-4o scores 56.57% overall where chance is 50% (Table, p.7). But reasoning models do much better in the same table: o3-mini (high) 80.86%, o1-preview 75.43%, DeepSeek-R1 73.14% (p.7-8). 'They' generalises from the non-reasoning judges to all.

suggested_wording: ... and on difficult objective comparisons many do little better than chance [@tan2025judgebench], ...
facts_to_cite: 350 response pairs, one objectively correct and one incorrect response each (p.3)
many strong models (e.g., GPT-4o) perform just slightly better than random guessing (p.1)
overlap_with_engtrace: Supports keeping the judge's role small and its precision measured. EngTrace's judge (MiMo-V2.5-Pro) is not asked to compare responses; it decides whether a trace reaches a value it is given, which is closer to the reference-given setting of krumdick2026nofreelabels than to JudgeBench's reference-free pairs. No change to the positioning claim.
notes: The venue is confirmed by the paper's own header. The results cited are from v2 (April 2025), which added reasoning models; the original version's weaker numbers are the source of the abstract's framing.
